cautions: LITERACY LEVEL: explain what each concept is, why it matters, and how to think about it. Do not teach tool-specific workflows (no pandas/NumPy/scikit-learn tutorials), do not require math beyond basic intuition, and do not turn any topic into a practitioner course.

TIME-ANCHOR AI CLAIMS: model capabilities, benchmark numbers, and tool names change quickly. Phrase claims as of the cited source date; never state capabilities as timeless facts. For generative-ai, large-language-models, and prompting-basics, use the model providers' own public documentation plus at least one independent source.

DEFINITIONAL DISTINCTIONS MUST BE KEPT CLEAN: structured vs unstructured data; supervised vs unsupervised learning; training vs testing data; correlation vs causation (correlation topic owns this); overfitting vs underfitting; bias as a statistical property vs bias as a fairness concern (bias and algorithmic-fairness are separate topics — keep them distinct).

HALLUCINATIONS AND EVALUATION: hallucinations are a documented failure mode of LLMs (stated factually, with the provider/scholar source); evaluating-ai-output owns how to check AI output; do not overclaim what current systems can or cannot do.
PRIVACY AND ETHICS: ai-privacy and ai-ethics are separate topics; keep the NIST RMF framing for ai-ethics and nist-ai-risk-concepts; no individualized legal, security, or medical advice.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic. Verify keys yourself from the file, and avoid reusing identical question-stem templates across topics.
